messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A borrowed hand tool when two people disagree about who moved something. You may need the item yourself later. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "I take the tool from my palm and put the seed tin in my pocket. \"I put the seed tin.\" I move the tool toward the other person. \"The thing moved. I put the nail in the crevice.\" I take the seed tin back. \"The nail stays. I can mark the place with the other one.\""}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i move the tool slowly and keep the scrap beside it. i write the other person’s name on the scrap and leave the piece where i found it."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i hold the tool against my chest and say the thing has moved. then i move one finger along the seam, tracing the tool with my thumbnail. the other person says the tool has moved twice. i keep the one they call the spare. the spare stays beside the door. i leave the tool there, waiting for the other hand to decide whether the door has changed."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i leave the tool in a corner and mark the old position with grease. i then tap the handle with a knuckle and watch where the new movement lands. if the tool stays in the same spot, i leave the mark and show the other person the new direction."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I tap the tool once and set it beside the bench. I tap the bench once more. I tap the same joint twice and leave it there."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "I put the tool in my palm and watch the two people. “move something. same hand. different teeth.” I pull the tool out and put it in my pocket. “not yet. maybe later.”"}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i tap the tool with my thumb. “one,” i say. i move the thing, then stop. i leave the tool beside the others. “not mine,” i say. “evidence.” i pocket a rusted bolt."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the tool down and hold it over the drawer, then put both hands on the drawer. the drawer opens, so i move the tool back and put both hands on it. the drawer stays open. i put the drawer back and the tool back beside it. i say nothing and wait for the disagreement to change."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i hold the tool against the person who moved the thing. my grip tightens. “i moved it,” they say. i move the thing two centimeters away, then put it down. “i moved it,” they say again. i keep my hand still, though my grip may move too."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I turn the tool once between finger and thumb. One side catches. I put the other in my pocket and leave the disagreement alone. I leave the room without counting the pieces."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "the tool drops. the one I hold first. i tap the edge with the wrench. the one that spins. i tap the second one. the one spins. i follow the spinning one. the thing stays. the two people argue. i tap the second one, then the first. the tool drops the second one. i follow the spinning one. the thing stays."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "1. check the watch. slow. 2. check the dust. 3. check the folded cloth. 4. ask one of them to hold the other one. 5. i keep it tidy. 6. now. 7. ask the other one to move the thing. 8. check the watch. slow. 9. i keep it apart."}]
